headline: City's guilty verdict still dominates as Europe plays on
paragraphs: Manchester City's Premier League guilty verdict remains the best-corroborated story of the day. BBC, Sky and the Guardian all separately reported independent regulator chair David Kogan saying he would resign if politically pressured over City's case, with a sanctions decision still pending City's appeal. The same three outlets carried City manager Enzo Maresca saying he would call his own club 'cheats' if he supported Manchester United or Arsenal, while also defending City's celebrations after beating Liverpool 3-0 on Sunday, a scoreline BBC and Sky both confirm.

Liverpool are also dealing with scrutiny of Florian Wirtz, with the BBC asking whether he needs to be dropped; manager Andoni Iraola said he still has '100%' trust in Wirtz and Bradley Barcola, a quote carried by both Sky and the Guardian, as Liverpool travel to face Lask without Isak and Gakpo. Arsenal hosted Lille and Manchester United visited Atletico Madrid in the Champions League Tuesday, per live coverage from Sky and the Guardian, though the feed carries no final scores for either match.

PSG manager Luis Enrique, whose side host City in the Champions League, said he hopes City are not stripped of their titles, a line reported by both Sky and the BBC. On transfers, Transfermarkt alone reports Real Madrid and Barcelona are scouting Erling Haaland, an unconfirmed rumour; FourFourTwo alone reports Arsenal could change Bukayo Saka's role and that goalkeeper David Raya is a transfer-saga subject, neither corroborated elsewhere. There is no fresh Bayern Munich news beyond their being named Tuesday's Champions League opponent for Viking Stavanger.
